claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has a native thin oxide film formed during standard processing.
The native oxide film on Q235 steel is composed primarily of iron oxides.
Fe2O3 and Fe3O4 are constituents of the native oxide film on Q235 steel.
The native oxide film provides Q235 steel with some corrosion protection at ambient and moderate temperatures.
Aggressive salt mixtures are molten and chemically reactive under the proposed 700–900 °C exposure regime.
Molten salt at 700–900 °C penetrates the native oxide film on Q235 steel.
Molten salt at 700–900 °C dissolves or chemically modifies the native oxide film.
Disruption of the native oxide film causes loss of its protective barrier function.
Loss of the oxide barrier makes the underlying Q235 steel more vulnerable to corrosion and degradation.
Q235 steel exposed to molten salt at 700–900 °C will show a higher rate of mass change than Q235 steel heated without molten salt.
Q235 steel exposed to molten salt at 700–900 °C will show greater surface degradation than Q235 steel heated without molten salt.
Q235 steel exposed to molten salt at 700–900 °C will show lower hardness than Q235 steel heated without molten salt.
At lower temperatures where the salt is not aggressively molten, the native oxide film will remain intact.
At room temperature or lower-temperature conditions without aggressive molten-salt behavior, the oxide film's protective effect is maintained.
Variations in the initial oxide-film characteristics can affect the extent of Q235 degradation.
